title: KV fragmentation budget & cross-region priming plan
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a conservative proposal for how we budget and prime KV cache during multi-region model onboards to minimize fragmentation and avoid cross-region eviction storms. Focus is on: (a) fragmentation metrics to track, (b) per-region priming budget allocation, (c) warmup backoff heuristics, and (d) expected GPU headroom impact for rollout scheduling.

Context / problem statement:
- New large encoder-decoder models and several customer variants (long-context, chat-history caching) increase KV entry count and variability.
- Naive warmup by uniformly priming top-N prefixes per region leads to uneven occupancy and high fragmentation (many small entries), causing elevated eviction churn and tail latency.
- Cross-region priming (duplicating prefixes in multiple regions) is sometimes necessary for routing resilience but multiplies cache footprint.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Median KV entry size: 1.8 KB (tokens + metadata); 95p: 6.5 KB for long contexts.
- Typical active prefixes per customer: 12–30.
- Default eviction policy: LRU with coarse-grained segment shards (128MB stripes).
- Target safety margin: keep warmup allocation <= 18% of region KV capacity to preserve headroom.

Key metrics to track (tracking sheet / alerting hooks):
- KV_fragmentation_ratio = (# entries < 512B) / total_entries per region
- Primed_duplication_factor = avg(# regions where prefix is primed)
- Eviction_rate_per_minute (post-warmup) by model_tag and region
- Median_eviction_latency (ms) and tail99_eviction_latency
- Warmup_success_rate: % of primed prefixes hit within T=30s of roll traffic

Per-region priming budget heuristics (proposal):
- Step 0: Compute region_capacity_GB from infra dashboard (current available KV RAM after OS/agent overhead).
- Step 1: Warmup_pool_GB = floor(region_capacity_GB * 0.14) (conservative baseline)
- Step 2: Per-model_pool = min(model_estimated_priming_GB, Warmup_pool_GB * model_share) where model_share is proportional to expected QPS contribution (from rollout plan).
- Step 3: Cap duplication: Primed_duplication_factor_target = 1.35 (only duplicate high-affinity prefixes across regions; avoid full duplication).

Example illustrative table (estimates):
Region | Est. KV entries (k) | Avg entry size (KB) | Priming budget (GB) | Duplication factor target | Est. GPU headroom impact (slot-equivalents)
us-west-2 | 4200 | 1.8 | 6.0 | 1.2 | 3
eu-central-1 | 3100 | 2.0 | 4.0 | 1.4 | 2
asia-east-1 | 1800 | 2.4 | 2.4 | 1.5 | 1
notes: headroom impact expressed as rough number of pre-reserved GPU slots (1 slot ≈ ability to host X concurrent requests depending on model).

Fragmentation controls (implementation suggestions):
- Bucketize prefixes by length / TTL and apply per-bucket admission limits so many small prefixes don't monopolize stripes.
- When admit_count(bucket) > threshold, only admit every Nth new prefix (sampling) and log as cold_fail for later background seeding.
- Compacting pass: run a low-priority compaction to coalesce small shards every 6h (best-effort) to reduce stripe fragmentation.

Cross-region priming policy (rules engine):
1) Primary affinity: always prime in the model’s primary region(s) up to per-model pool.
2) Failover-critical prefixes: tag prefixes classified as 'failover-critical' (metrics: top-20 prefixes by tail impact) — allow duplication up to factor 2 but only after satisfying local warmup.
3) Regional risk throttle: if region_eviction_rate > baseline * 1.5, immediately halt cross-region duplication for 1h and start exponential backoff for further duplication.
4) Staggered priming window: when rolling model across N regions, schedule priming windows with random jitter (0–12m) to avoid synchronized bursts hitting global kv backend.

Warmup backoff heuristic (for staged rollouts):
- Phase A (canary): prime 10% of predicted hot prefixes; measure hit rate in 15m; if eviction_rate delta <= +10% and warmup_success_rate >= 70%, proceed to Phase B.
- Phase B (regional expansion): multiply primed set by x3 across top QPS customers but cap duplication factor at target. Monitor for 60m.
- Phase C (global release): allow remaining prefixes but run continuous sampling to evict low-value primed prefixes after 24h.

Expected GPU headroom modeling (quick formula):
- delta_KV_GB = sum_regions(primed_GB_region * duplication_factor_region)
- slot_impact = ceil(delta_KV_GB / GB_per_slot) where GB_per_slot is typical KV footprint per GPU slot (measured per model class).
- Example: If delta_KV_GB = 12.4GB and GB_per_slot = 2.8GB then slot_impact = 5 slots.

Operational runbook (short):
- Pre-roll checklist (owner: Aisha):
  - snapshot region_capacity_GB and current_eviction_rate (take before-priming baseline)
  - compute priming plan CSV (region, model, primed_GB, duplication_target) and upload to rollout ticket
  - schedule staggered priming windows and notify SRE on-call
- During roll (owner: on-call SRE):
  - watch Eviction_rate_per_min; if it exceeds baseline * 2 -> abort further priming and trigger rollback hook
  - if Primed_duplication_factor > target by >0.2 -> throttle cross-region replication
- Post-roll (owner: model-owner + infra):
  - run fragmentation ratio report at 1h, 6h, 24h and create follow-up ticket if fragmentation > 0.35

Open questions / follow-ups:
- We need a lightweight probe to classify prefixes by "failover-critical" automatically — sync with solutions-eng to get customer SLAs indicator.
- How to quantitatively choose GB_per_slot across model families? propose synthetic sandbox runs and map measured KV footprint to GPU utilization.
- Add per-tenant priming quotas to avoid a single customer consuming warmup pool.

Immediate next actions (this week):
- [Aisha] upload per-region capacity snapshot and run the sample calculation for models scheduled next month (due 2026-03-10).
- [Jon] prototype admission sampling logic (PR #402) and document expected mem/CPU overhead.
- [Marta] instrument fragmentation_ratio metric in observability dashboard and create alert playbook.

Quick notes / rough math (kept for traceability):
- 4200k entries * 1.8KB ≈ 7.56 GB total index footprint; priming 800k of those (hot prefixes) => 800k * 1.8KB ≈ 1.44GB; duplication factor 1.3 => 1.87GB additional.
- Conservative rounding added to buffer (x1.1) to account for metadata and per-stripe overhead.

Bottom line: aim to automate admission and duplication controls so warmups are decoupled from rigid full replication. With a 14% warmup pool target and conservative duplication targets we should be able to onboard medium-sized models (10–20M prefix space) without materially reducing GPU serving headroom, provided we enforce sampling and shard compaction.

Document history / notes: this is a working draft for the Q2 onboard cadence and is intentionally conservative. Expected to iterate after prototyping admission sampling.
